claims.text: The homogenized Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy initially has a dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial FCC/B2 interfaces are incoherent.
The initial alloy has high strength but is brittle.
Stress concentration at the incoherent interfaces causes the initial brittleness.
The proposed intervention is a hexahedron-anvil HPHT treatment at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours.
The HPHT treatment will topologically transform the FCC/B2 lamellae.
The treatment will convert incoherent interfaces into coherent interfaces within a hierarchically patterned microstructure.
Coherent FCC/B2 interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between the two phases.
The transformed structure promotes dislocation glide, stacking-fault formation, and twinning.
Dislocation transfer and the additional deformation mechanisms produce a more homogeneous strain distribution.
Homogeneous strain distribution alleviates interfacial stress concentrations and arrests interfacial cracking.
The treatment will significantly increase ductility.
The ductility increase will occur without substantial loss of strength.
The treated alloy will exhibit elongated crack propagation on its fracture surface.
The GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge at high strain after treatment.
The untreated alloy exhibits isolated microcracks at incoherent interfaces.
The untreated alloy develops divergent GND densities between the FCC and B2 phases under strain.
The useful processing window must drive interface transformation while remaining below the threshold for phase instability or eutectic decomposition.
HPHT is known to enhance diffusion and interface coherence in other material systems.
At the proposed conditions, pressure may instead induce a BCC, amorphous, or other undesired phase transformation.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that the transformed interfaces arrest interfacial cracking, whereas the proposed positive fracture-surface signature is elongated crack propagation. Without clarification that elongation represents stable or noninterfacial cracking, these statements are in tension.
